newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-QBE more confident on yr profit growth.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-QBE more confident on yr profit growth.

text.p: QBE Insurance Group Ltd was more confident of posting strong profit growth in the year to June 30 than it was at the time of its annual meeting in October last year, QBE's managing director John Cloney said on Monday.
"I'm more confident (on full year earnings growth). The reason I say that is because reinsurance has given us a huge punch in profit," Cloney told reporters at a media briefing.

Cloney said the reinsurance division's substantial growth and profit from new initiatives had more than made up for the higher competition in the insurance business in Australia and lower than expected growth from its Asian operation.
At the October annual meeting, Cloney said QBE expected profit growth of between 10 and 20 percent in the year to June 30, 1997 with growth possibly in the high teens.
Cloney said stiff competition meant the company was forecasting general insurance premium income growth of only 10 percent from its Australia operations in 1996/97.

Premium income growth from QBE's international operations was also seen up by 10 percent in 1996/97 with a slowdown in growth in Hong Kong in the first half being counterbalanced by strong growth from Indonesia, Thailand and Malaysia.

Cloney said the Hong Kong insurance market saw higher competition from Chinese insurance companies in the lead up to the June 30 handover and because the Bank of China had recently started its own insurance operation.
"We think we see some light at the end of the tunnel with the Hong Kong slowdown, but it's a bit early to call yet," Cloney said.
Cloney said the company was very pleased with the U.K. reinsurance operations of Allstate Insurance Co which it acquired for A$70 million in September last year.
"It's all going pretty much to plan. It takes a little time because you have to grapple with integration of people and systems but that it is all going along pretty well," Cloney said.

Since the acquisition, QBE has changed the name of the Allstate operation to QBE Reinsurance and shortened the maturity of the division's investment portfolio which consisted entirely of fixed interest securities.
The company said earlier that QBE Reinsurance had produced an after tax profit of A$7.6 million in the first half.
Cloney said QBE could handle a substantial purchase and was constantly assessing new opportunities but was not on the verge of announcing any acquisitions.

QBE saw most acquisition opportunities outside of Australia snd said Europe was looking more attractive because of changes caused by deregulation and the emerging reinsurance market in Eastern Europe.
